# P15 Visual material

- Requirement: Conditionally required when judgment depends on seeing a screen or behavior. If capture is unavailable, record the missing attachment and who should confirm it
- Placement: Attachments at the end
- Narrative role: Places original captures, full responses and attached diagrams at the end.
- Author: Observer or person explaining the flow
- Reviewer: The observing team for actual screens; the team owning each step for relationships and sequence
- Check: Are actual captures, originals, annotated copies and explanatory diagrams distinguished, and problem locations clearly marked with borders and numbers? Are GIF reproduction order, static alternatives, sensitive information and inclusion appropriate?

<!-- body:start -->
## Attachments

**[Material title and nature].** Explain [whether it is an actual capture, screen recording, code or logs, or explanatory diagram] and [the problem or judgment it shows]. Point to this material with a note in the relevant body text.

If the actual screen can be captured, record [environment, build, time and reproduction conditions], and distinguish the image as captured from the annotated copy. On the annotated copy, add borders that do not obscure the problem area, numbers and short explanations. Do not convey meaning through color alone.

If the sequence of behavior is central, attach a short GIF or recording showing [clicks, waits and malfunction], and also provide decisive frames as static images. If material is unavailable, record the missing attachment, who should confirm it and the necessary access conditions. Do not use an expected screen or explanatory GIF as evidence of actual observation.
<!-- body:end -->
